subject: Throughput degradation: adaptive fallbacks and customer update
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [Incident] BrightCart throughput drop — initial triage + asks

Team,

We just saw a sustained throughput drop (~35%) and p95 generation latency doubling for BrightCart's gen-api traffic in us-west-2 starting ~08:58 PDT. Impact window correlates with a fanout spike (many short requests) from their checkout flow. Early signals: autoscaler scaled but headroom saturated, KV cache eviction rate spiked, and kernel scheduling latencies climbed in the runtime.

Attached: perf_snapshot_0608.log (short), autoscaler-metrics-0608.png.

Immediate asks:
- Ben/SRE: can you triage kernel scheduling vs. KV eviction root cause? Quick mitigations we should consider: temporary routing rule to dedicated pool, increase autoscaler headroom, or apply token fanout throttling at the routing layer.
- Product (Marissa): we need guidance on acceptable fallbacks for BrightCart (canary routing to dedicated vs. universal fallback). Avoiding collateral impact for other customers is high priority.
- Eng (Karthik): if we need to bump KV cache TTL or change eviction thresholds, what's the risk window? Can we do a short-lived config change safely?
- Customer comm: we'll need a 1-paragraph customer-facing note to send to Liz/Tue morning ASAP.

Proposed immediate plan (fast):
1) Apply routing rule to siphon up to 20% of BrightCart traffic to a dedicated pool (10–30 min change).
2) Temporarily increase autoscaler headroom by +15% for the three impacted nodes.
3) If eviction continues, flip a config to increase KV TTL for their tenant to reduce cold-start hits (requires Karthik sign-off).

Please ack and call out which item you can own; I can draft the customer note once we agree on mitigation.

-Neha

Attachment stubs: perf_snapshot_0608.log (text), autoscaler-metrics-0608.png (image)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Incident] BrightCart throughput drop — initial triage + asks

On Tue, Jun 8, 2027 at 09:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> We just saw a sustained throughput drop (~35%) and p95 generation latency doubling for BrightCart's gen-api traffic in us-west-2

Thanks — quick update from the SRE side after a 20m look:
- Kernel scheduling backlog on a subset of pods: long tail in GPU-to-CPU sync. This explains increased per-token CPU waits.
- KV cache shows a churn pattern consistent with a sharp increase in short-lived requests (token fanout). TTLs are default; eviction rate spiked ~3x at 08:58.
- Autoscaler reacted but policy has a 2-min cooldown and the current allocation was insufficient for the burst shape.

Immediate actions I can take in the next 30m:
1) Push a routing rule (rbac+policy check done) to route up to 15% of BrightCart traffic to the dedicated gpu-pool-d1. Risk: small QPS shift; will monitor cross-tenant interference.
2) Increase autoscaler headroom to +20% for affected node group (no deployment required).
3) Deploy a temporary token-fanout soft-throttle at the routing layer for heavy short requests (limits option). This is low-risk and buys us ~10–20% throughput improvement for the overall cluster.

I recommend we apply 1 + 2 immediately, 3 if we still see p95 > target in 15–30m. Karthik, if you can sign off on a brief KV TTL bump for BrightCart, that will reduce cold misses — but it requires a tenant-level config change and coordination with cache ops.

Attaching: perf_snapshot_0608.log (short extract) — highlights eviction timestamps.

-ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Incident] BrightCart throughput drop — immediate plan + customer note draft

Thanks Ben — that approach sounds right. A few product trade-offs to call out:
- Routing to dedicated will change latency profiles slightly (warmer KV) but may cause capacity pressure if we fully shift traffic. Start canary at 10% and move to 50% only if metrics improve.
- Fanout soft-throttle is preferable to blunt capacity pressure without changing routing. It may increase latency for a tiny fraction of requests but will protect overall SLOs.
- Increasing KV TTL for BrightCart is a good medium-term mitigation (reduces churn) but we should limit to a 6-hour window to measure impact.

Customer note draft (send this after we apply mitigations):
-----
Hi Liz,

We're investigating a performance regression affecting BrightCart's checkout generation traffic in us-west-2. We're implementing a targeted mitigation (routing a small portion of your traffic to dedicated capacity and applying throttling for very short high-fanout requests). We expect this to restore throughput within ~30–60 minutes with minimal impact to request quality. We'll follow up with a brief incident summary and any recommended configuration changes on our side.

If you have constraints about routing or notice any immediate business impact, please reply and we'll pause the change.

Thanks for the quick heads-up — we’ll update you in ~30 minutes.

Best,
Neha (on behalf of Redwood Ops)
-----

Action owners:
- Ben: apply routing + autoscaler bump (go/no-go in 15m).
- Soojin: prepare monitoring dashboard with p95/p50, eviction rate, and kernel schedule tail.
- Karthik: prepare KV TTL change plan (6-hour window) and short rollback steps.

Marissa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Liz Turner <liz@brightcart.com>
Cc: BrightCart SRE <sre-team@brightcart.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Briefing: temporary routing & mitigation for latency event

Hi Liz — quick note from Redwood Ops: we observed an increase in short high-fanout requests from your checkout flow starting ~08:58 PDT that caused elevated p95 latency and a throughput drop in us-west-2.

Planned immediate mitigation (targeting restoration within 30–60m):
- Route up to 10% of checkout generation requests to a dedicated pool to reduce cross-tenant interference.
- Apply a soft throttle for extremely short, high-fanout requests to reduce churn on KV cache.

Expected impact: brief (<5%) quality variance on a very small subset of requests while mitigations stabilize throughput. No change to stored data or retention.

If you prefer we hold and continue diagnosis without routing changes, please let us know. Otherwise we’ll proceed in ~10 minutes and I’ll update you once metrics are stable.

-Neha Kapoor
Senior Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Liz Turner <liz@brightcart.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightCart SRE <sre-team@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Briefing: temporary routing & mitigation for latency event

Neha — thanks for the heads-up and the clear plan. Please proceed with the mitigations. We prefer you proceed rather than risk longer checkout failures. Keep us posted on the timeline and any short-term impacts we should look out for.

— Liz

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Incident] BrightCart throughput drop — mitigation applied and status

Update: we applied the routing canary (10%) + autoscaler headroom + soft fanout throttle at 15:30 PDT. Since the change:
- Throughput improved back to ~96% of baseline within ~12 minutes.
- p95 generation latency dropped to near-target (p95 reduced ~40% vs. peak).
- KV eviction rate returned to normal ranges.

Ben, can you confirm any kernel scheduling residuals still visible? Karthik, please proceed with the 6-hour KV TTL bump tonight at 18:00 if eviction remains stable — watch rollback plan defined in the runbook.

I'll start the incident postmortem doc and assign follow-ups (infra config, autoscaler tuning, product gating for routing fallbacks). Closing immediate operational loop.

-Soojin
